info.howDoLegacyEncodingsDifferFromStandardUn: How do legacy encodings differ from standard Unicode?
info.beforeWidespreadUnicodeSupportSinhalaFon: Before widespread Unicode support, Sinhala fonts mapped glyphs to ASCII positions. FM Abhaya, FM Malithi, and DL-Manel are examples of these non-Unicode fonts. This encoding is still found in documents, publishing files, and digital archives.
info.bothFontTypesCanDisplayTheSameSinhalaTex: Both font types can display the same Sinhala text, but store it differently. Legacy encodings store ASCII characters mapped to glyphs; Unicode stores standard Sinhala characters. Without the right font, legacy text may appear as Latin letters or symbols and is difficult to search, analyze, or translate automatically.
info.theStoredDataIsAsciiWithoutTheCorrespond: The stored data is ASCII. Without the corresponding font, the underlying characters are shown instead of Sinhala glyphs.
info.sinhalafontsNetHasFmAbhayaFmMalithiFmGem: SinhalaFonts.net has FM Abhaya, FM Malithi, FM Gemunu, FM Bindumathi, and other legacy FM fonts, with previews and downloads. Availability on a third-party site does not imply an open license; follow each font's own terms.
info.pitakaLkProvidesUnicodeVersionsThatPrese: Pitaka.lk provides Unicode versions that preserve traditional FM designs while supporting standard Sinhala text. Fonts are available for download and installation; commercial use still requires the appropriate permission.
info.modernOperatingSystemsUsuallyIncludeSinh: Modern operating systems usually include Sinhala fonts. The text uses standard Unicode Sinhala characters with defined meaning.
info.defaultFontsVaryByOperatingSystemCommonC: Default fonts vary by operating system. Common choices are listed below.
info.nirmalaUiIsASansSerifUiFontForWindows: Nirmala UI is a sans-serif UI font for Windows 8 and later. Iskoola Pota has a more traditional text style and was the earlier Windows default for Sinhala. Since Windows 10, it is a supplemental Sinhala font, usually installed with language support.
info.sinhalaSangamMnHasAModernUiStyleWhileSin: Sinhala Sangam MN has a modern UI style, while Sinhala MN has a traditional text style. Apple supplies both but does not explicitly define them as a serif/sans-serif fallback pair.
info.notoSansSinhalaIsUsuallyTheMainSinhalaFa: Noto Sans Sinhala is usually the main Sinhala fallback. Noto Serif Sinhala is explicitly a serif fallback in AOSP. Android vendors may change the configuration, so the actual fonts can vary.
info.itConvertsTheStoredCharacterDataBetweenU: It converts the stored character data between Unicode and legacy font encodings.
info.convertingLegacyTextToUnicodeRemovesItsD: Converting legacy text to Unicode removes its dependence on a particular old font and makes it easier to display, store, search, copy, translate, and process as Sinhala. Reverse conversion produces ASCII sequences for older publishing software, documents, and workflows that still rely on FM or DL fonts.
info.thisIsNotAOneToOneAsciiSubstitutionLegac: This is not a one-to-one ASCII substitution. Legacy fonts often store characters in visual order, while Unicode uses logical order. Conversion identifies consonants, vowel signs, joiners, abbreviations, and conjuncts and reorders them. Reverse conversion rebuilds the glyph sequence expected by legacy typography.
info.theExamplesBelowShowLegacyGlyphsOnTheLef: The examples below show legacy glyphs on the left and Unicode text on the right. Choose “Show encoding” to see the characters behind the legacy glyphs.
info.reorderLegacyVowelSignsIntoUnicodeCharac: Reorder legacy vowel signs into Unicode character order.
info.recognizeConjunctsAndPrenasalizedConsona: Recognize conjuncts and prenasalized consonants, with dedicated ද glyphs when compact forms are enabled.
info.recognizeFormsSuchAsTrailingLowerAndUppe: Recognize forms such as trailing ය, lower ර, and upper ර built with virama and joiners.

info.convertOnlySinhalaSegmentsPreservingEngl: Convert only Sinhala segments, preserving English, numbers, and other text.

info.differentLegacyInputOrdersForTheSameGlyp: Different legacy input orders for the same glyph normalize to the same Unicode sequence.

notes.legacyFontsUsuallyDoNotSupportStraightQu: Legacy fonts usually do not support straight quotes; conversion replaces them with curly quotes.
notes.legacyFontsLackDedicatedAndConjunctsThes: Legacy fonts lack dedicated ්‍රු and ්‍රූ conjuncts; these are expanded to ්රු and ්රූ.
notes.legacyFontsLackDedicatedAndGlyphsSoThese: Legacy fonts lack dedicated ඞ, ඞි, and ඞී glyphs, so these cannot be converted to legacy encoding.
notes.theLegacyCodeForWorksOnlyInSomeFontsAnd: The legacy code for ඣ් works only in some fonts and may display incorrectly in others.
notes.touchingLettersHaveNoDedicatedLegacyCode: Touching letters have no dedicated legacy codes; conversion expands them into ordinary letter sequences and cannot preserve the touching form.
notes.unicodeDocumentsExportedInEitherModeUseS: Unicode documents exported in either mode use system fonts rather than custom fonts, with Iskoola Pota as a fallback.
notes.documentModeExtractsSelectableTextOnlyOr: Document mode extracts selectable text only. Original layout and formatting are not preserved; output is always DOCX.

avalon.description: Find Merlin with friends. A 5–10 player game of hidden roles, team votes and quests.

night.peek: Turn it over. Only you can see it

avalon.discussionHintSelf: You are the leader for this round.
avalon.beginTeam: End discussion and build a team

avalon.guideInvite: 1. Create a room and share the invitation. Each player joins in their own browser.
avalon.guideDiscuss: 2. Discuss over your preferred voice app. The website deals roles, collects votes and resolves quests.
avalon.guideWin: 3. Good must complete three quests and protect Merlin. Evil can win by sabotaging quests or rejecting five teams in a row.

night.detail: Roles are dealt randomly. Privately view your role and any players you may know. Daybreak starts once everyone confirms.

discussion.title: Round-by-round discussion
discussion.detail: Slow round: everyone may speak freely. Fast round: the leader invites one player for a two-person conversation. The leader may end the discussion early.

team.title: The leader selects a team
team.detail: The leader selects quest members according to the team-size table below.

vote.title: Everyone votes
vote.detail: Players approve or reject the team. A majority must approve to proceed; otherwise a new leader starts another discussion. Five consecutive rejections give Evil the win.

quest.title: Carry out the quest in secret
quest.detail: Team members play quest cards. Good must Execute; Evil may Execute or Sabotage. Usually one Sabotage card is enough to fail the quest.

evilDiscussion.title: Assassination discussion
evilDiscussion.detail: After three successful quests, all roles remain secret. Anyone may speak or reveal their own role.

victory.title: Decide the winner
victory.detail: Three failed quests give Evil the win. After three successes, the Assassin locks in one target: finding Merlin wins for Evil; otherwise Good wins.

rulebook.sequenceHint: Hover over or tap a quest card to see its team size and special rule.
rulebook.night: Roles are assigned at random. At night, privately view your role and anyone you are allowed to know. Daybreak begins once everyone confirms.
rulebook.discussion: Each round begins with discussion. In a slow round, everyone can speak for 30 seconds per player. In a fast round, the leader has 15 seconds to invite one player, followed by a 60-second dialogue. Team selection begins when time runs out or the leader ends discussion early.
rulebook.team: The leader selects a quest team of the size shown below. Submitting the team automatically records the leader's approval.
rulebook.vote: Other players secretly approve or reject. The team proceeds only with more than half the votes; a tie rejects it. Five consecutive rejections give Evil the win.
rulebook.quest: Only quest members secretly play cards. Good players must Execute; Evil players may Execute or Sabotage. Usually one Sabotage card fails the quest.
rulebook.victory: Three failed quests give Evil the win. After three successful quests, the Assassin names Merlin: a correct guess wins for Evil, otherwise Good wins.
rulebook.teamSizes: Teams and quest sizes by player count
rulebook.twoFails: With 7 or more players, the fourth quest needs at least two Sabotage cards to fail.

reasons.rejections: Five teams were rejected in a row. Evil wins.
reasons.merlin: The Assassin found Merlin. Evil wins.
reasons.assassination: Three quests succeeded and Merlin survived. Good wins.
reasons.aborted: The host ended the game. There is no winner.
